title: Per-credential SLA + Degradation Matrix (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working doc to capture UX thinking for per-credential and per-route rate limiting/quota surfaces, focused on: (1) a degradation matrix for SLA tiers, (2) per-API-key and per-route breakdown cards, and (3) how we explain 'why throttled' to customers.

Context / motivation:
- Ops teams need a single place to understand which keys/routes are most at risk of hitting limits and what degraded behavior looks like per SLA tier.
- Developers and platform owners want actionable next steps (reduce qps, switch to dedicated, request burst) rather than raw numbers.
- Current console has only coarse quotas and a generic throttling banner — not enough to debug cross-key spikes or to present clear remediation.

High-level UX goals (non-exhaustive):
- Present a degradation matrix that maps traffic percentiles -> user-visible effects (timeouts, 429s, soft-throttle, increased latency, fallback model selection).
- Surface per-key and per-route heatmaps with actionable signals and a short explanation line for each anomaly.
- Provide an explainer modal for each throttle event: root cause candidate (rate limiter, burst window, quota burn), recovery ETA, recommended mitigations.

Wireframe idea (top-to-bottom):
1) Top filters row: Time window (15m/1h/6h/24h/7d), Region, Deployment (hosted/dedicated/private), Model family.
2) SLA selector pill: dropdown to pick customer SLA profile (free/trial/standard/premium/custom). Changes degradation matrix and recommended mitigations.
3) Degradation matrix visualization (left): a 4x5 grid. Columns = percent-of-capacity (0-20%, 20-50%, 50-80%, 80-100%, >100%). Rows = severity bands (info/warning/critical/blackout). Each cell shows an icon and short copy (e.g., 80-100% / critical => "Increased 95th latency, intermittent 429s"). Clicking a cell opens example user-facing symptoms and sample telemetry.
4) Right column: per-key leaderboard (top 10 keys by tokens consumed). Each row: credential id (masked), owner/team tag, sparkline (token/sec), current burn rate %, estimated time to quota at current rate, actions (snooze alert, increase quota, view traces).
5) Below: per-route exploded view. Route cards with mini-heatmap of 99p latency, avg tokens, 429 rate, and top contributing keys. Routes can be expanded to show recent example requests (anonymized) and prompt size distributions.
6) Alert timeline at bottom: chronological list of throttle events with one-click link to related key & route cards.

Microcopy and affordances (notes):
- Credential rows: show masked key (rxa***45) and owner if available (link to team page). When owner unknown show a CTA "Assign owner" that opens a modal with suggested owners based on recent commits / last modified.
- 'Why throttled?' tooltip: one-line root cause + "How to fix" quick action. Example: "Throttled by short-window burst limit. Try smoothing requests with client-side jitter or request burst increase (request form)."
- Examples for degraded behavior should use customer-facing language (no infra jargon) + a collapsible section with raw signals.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- New "Rate Insights" page under Quotas/Usage that loads in < 1s for accounts with <= 1k keys.
- Degradation matrix shows mapped symptoms for >= 90% of known limiter states.
- Per-key leaderboard includes: masked key, owner, tokens/sec, burn %, est time to quota, and direct link to increase quota request.
- Each throttle event in timeline links to at least one key and one route.
- Explanations provide a suggested remediation and a prefilled support form when appropriate.

Backlog grooming (candidate tickets):
- PRD-1107: Build degradation matrix component + copy library. (priority: high)
- ENG-4812: Backend: expose per-key per-route aggregated signals (1m,5m,1h windows) + root-cause hints. (priority: high)
- UX-1899: Wireframe: per-key card interactions + owner assignment flow. (priority: medium)
- SRE-2051: Define sample retention policy for throttle diagnostics (retain request ids for 7 days). (priority: medium)
- DATA-3320: Add estimator for "time-to-quota" based on EWMA of recent burn rate. (priority: low)

Telemetry and signals (for engineering):
- required metrics: token_count, request_count, 429_count, avg_latency_95p, kv_cache_hit_rate, model_variant_fallback_count.
- derived signals: burn_rate_pct (vs quota), ewma_tokens_per_min, burst_window_violation (binary), concurrent_streams_count.

Edge cases & open questions:
- How to handle keys shared across multiple teams? Proposed: allow multi-owner tags and show "primary owner" heuristic (most recent commit / usage).
- Can we meaningfully estimate impact of KV cache hits on throttles? Need infra input. Ticket: SRE-2059.
- Internationalization of microcopy: decide if symptom text should be i18n-ready at MVP or deferred.
- Data volume: for customers with >10k keys, the leaderboard should default to top N by burn or allow a full export.

Copy library (short examples):
- Cell (80-100% / critical): "Experiencing intermittent 429s. Latency may increase for long prompts. Consider limiting burst or moving heavy workloads to Dedicated."
- Tooltip: "This key recently sent a sustained spike of requests in the last 5m. Example: 3x baseline traffic, 45% of error budget consumed."
- CTA button: "Request temporary burst" -> opens modal with suggested size and rationale (prefilled).

Prototype interaction notes (for devs):
- Clicking a per-key row opens split panel (right) with 24h timeline, top 5 routes for that key, and a "Replay" button to re-run a sample prompt against a sandbox model.
- When a user changes SLA pill, the degradation matrix should animate to show before/after comparisons and mark changed cells with a subtle pulse.

Operational concerns:
- UI must not surface full key values. Masking + last 4 chars only.
- Actions that change quotas must require RBAC: only org admins or billing owners can request increases.
- Audit log entry for every manual override or temp-burst approval.

Next steps / immediate to-dos:
- Sync w/ Diego + SRE (Priya) for exact signals exposed by ENG-4812 (this week).
- Quick study: identify top 100 customers with multi-key ownership for edge-case handling (DATA team).
- Build low-fi Figma frames for the leaderboard + matrix (assigned: Leah).
- Add examples to copy library and get legal review for support language.

Notes to self / rough ideas left in the doc:
- Consider a "Cost impact" column (est $/day at current burn) — useful for finance conversations.
- Explore auto-remediation: when a key hits 95% and owner unresponsive, auto-snooze non-critical traffic for 15m? Needs policy review.
- Think about exposing token attribution per function call (for apps using function/tool calling) — may help in root cause.

Last refs & forks:
- Look at Netlify/Cloudflare rate limit dashboards for inspiration on cell UI and incident timeline layout.
- The quota-forecasting doc links in Confluence (see linked artifacts) for modeling approach.

If reviewers: please add your quick comment under the section you touch, mark TODOs with [ACTION], and link any related Jira/PRs.

-- Maya
